usage:
# CSM Voice: text-to-audio with Transformers

This page is the Transformers contract of the CSM Voice MIC and also a usage example. The MIC runner runs the blocks below against each slim fixture and each checkpoint in [`integration.json`](../../integration.json).

## Forward pass (text → audio logits)

```py runnable:csm_voice
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, set_seed
import json  # doc-builder: hide
import os  # doc-builder: hide

model_id = "cartesia/azzurra-voice"
model_id = os.environ.get("MIC_MODEL", model_id)  # doc-builder: hide
variant = json.loads(os.environ.get("MIC_MODEL_KWARGS", "{}"))  # doc-builder: hide
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
set_seed(0)

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id).to(device)
if variant:  # doc-builder: hide
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, **variant).to(device)

prompts = ["Hello, how are you today?", "The weather is nice outside."]
inputs = tokenizer(prompts, return_tensors="pt", padding=True).to(device)

model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
logits = outputs.logits

# Compact probes: first 4 sequence positions, first 8 audio-vocab entries
audio_logits = logits[:, :4, :8].float().tolist()
print(f"logits shape: {tuple(logits.shape)}")
print(f"audio_logits: {audio_logits}")
```

## One training step

```py runnable:csm_voice:2
labels = torch.full(inputs["input_ids"].shape, -100, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
labels[0, 1:5] = torch.tensor([100, 200, 300, 400], device=device)
labels[1, 1:5] = torch.tensor([150, 250, 350, 450], device=device)

model.train()
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
loss = model(**inputs, labels=labels).loss
loss.backward()
before = {name: p.detach().clone() for name, p in model.named_parameters()}  # doc-builder: hide
optimizer.step()
print(f"loss: {loss.item():.4f}")

if os.environ.get("MIC_RUNNER"):  # doc-builder: hide
    named = dict(model.named_parameters())
    trainable = [n for n, p in named.items() if p.requires_grad]
    checked = trainable[:2]
    result = {
        "runtime": {
            "device": model.device.type,
            "dtype": str(model.dtype).removeprefix("torch."),
            "attn_implementation": model.config._attn_implementation,
        },
        "audio_logits": audio_logits,
        "training": {
            "loss": loss.item(),
            "gradients": {n: bool(named[n].grad is not None and torch.count_nonzero(named[n].grad) > 0 and torch.isfinite(named[n].grad).all()) for n in checked},
            "updated": any(not torch.equal(named[n], before[n]) for n in trainable),
        },
    }
    print(json.dumps(result))
```
rationale: CSM (Continuous Speech Model) is a text-conditioned audio generation model using a LLaMA-1B backbone and Mimi codec. The integration exercises the standard AutoModelForCausalLM path with text token input producing audio-vocabulary logits (2051 entries). Two distinct prompts with padding provide meaningful batch perturbation. Compact probes (4 positions × 8 vocab entries) keep output size small while remaining sensitive to weight changes. A real SGD training step with audio-token labels verifies gradient flow through the cross-vocabulary architecture (text input embeddings → LLaMA backbone → audio lm_head).

historical_candidates.reason: CsmForConditionalGeneration is a new architecture (transformers 5.1.0); AutoModelForCausalLM registration and forward signature for cross-vocabulary models (text input, audio output) may have edge cases with padding or the codec sub-module.
The Mimi codec sub-model (kyutai/mimi) embedded in the config may affect device placement or dtype casting when the parent model is moved to a non-CPU device or loaded in bfloat16.
